Principle 19: Culture
The Korean culture is different from other cultures.
It has many unique aspects about it.
Our clothes, housing, names, and language are not like
any other countries.
First, I would like to explain about traditional Korean clothing.
On ordinary occasions, Korean people wear Western style clothes.
However, on traditional holidays, families celebrate these days
by wearing traditional costumes called han-bok.
Another unique aspect of Korean culture is its food.
Traditional Korean meals usually include boiled rice, soup, fish or meat,
several vegetable side dishes, and one or more kinds of kimchi.
My favorite food is bulgogi.
Bulgogi is the most popular Korean meat dish,
while the most popular vegetable dish is kimchi.
I like them both.
Finally, the Korean language is not like any other world language.
Up until the middle of the 15th century,
Korea didn't have its own alphabet.
Instead, they Chinese characters were used in order to write.
Most people couldn't read or write.
The only people who could read were the scholars or the nobility.
However, in 1420, the current King at that time,
Se-jong, asked his royal scholars to create a unique Korean alphabet.
Soon a writing system known as hangul was created.
